content.comment_body: Hello, if I set the diagram version in the additional info section of [product_name] software, is it possible to view or read this version on the [product_name] hardware? What is the actual purpose of this information? Whenever I download the program from the [product_name] device to my PC, the version always appears as 1.0.0. Thank you!
I'm not entirely certain what you're referring to. Are you asking about a UDF? Please clarify with more details.

In the diagram properties under offline settings, there is an additional info section where you can set the version. I am trying to find out if this information can somehow be read to determine which version is stored in the [product_name] device. Thanks!

The online help states: 2.8.1.17 File -> Properties - Additional Info In this section, you can input details related to your current circuit program, including fields for project information, internal company data, and the version number of your circuit program. Instead of a text string for the company name, you can also specify an image file for your company logo to customize your program files. 6.6 How to identify your circuit program version You can set the version number of your circuit program in the Version field located in File → Properties: Additional Info (Page 61). [product_name] software retains version information during program downloads or uploads between your PC and the [product_name] device. If you have further questions, consider starting a support request.
I’ve read this, but what does "[product_name] software retains the version..." actually mean? There’s no explanation about how to read, display, or use this information.
I’m also not sure... That’s why I suggested starting a support request.

The version information is mainly for your reference as a programmer and is optional. It's included in the [product_name] software project but not transferred to the [product_name] hardware. The hardware doesn't use this for the diagram calculations. The version reference always comes from the offline project, not what's loaded on the hardware. Loading a program back from the hardware is just an emergency option if you've lost your offline project. It's best to keep backup copies of your offline work.

Thank you for clarifying. So, the only way to identify the loaded diagram is by using the Message texts block. It would be helpful if there was a way to read the diagram version directly from the [product_name] device or display it on the website interface.

analysis.insight_summary: Users are confused about the role and accessibility of the diagram version feature in [product_name] software. There is uncertainty regarding whether this version metadata can be accessed or viewed from the [product_name] hardware itself. Users have found that this information isn't typically transferred or easily retrievable, which limits its usefulness for version tracking during device operation.
analysis.user_expectations: Users expect that the diagram version set in [product_name] software should be accessible from the [product_name] hardware, or at least displayable on the device or via its web interface.
